key_insight: EVENET learns reusable patterns from simulated particle collisions and transfers them across multiple analysis tasks. Its ability to work on real collider data connects simulation-based training with experimental use.
problem_solved: Particle collision analysis needs models that generalize across tasks and bridge the gap between simulated training data and real experimental measurements.
method: Pretrain a foundation model, EVENET, on simulated particle collision data.
Combine self-supervised learning with supervision from physics labels.
Transfer the pretrained model across analysis tasks and apply it to real collider data.
impact: EVENET demonstrates how foundation-model pretraining can support scientific analysis beyond language and images. For AI/ML practitioners, it highlights the potential of combining self-supervision with domain-specific labels to build reusable models.
visual_elements: Pipeline: simulated collisions → EVENET pretraining → multiple analysis tasks.
Two training streams—self-supervised learning and physics labels—merging into one model.
Hub-and-spoke diagram showing EVENET supporting several downstream tasks.
Simulation-to-experiment bridge linking synthetic collision events to real collider measurements.
paper_title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
paper_authors: Ting-Hsiang Hsu, Baihong Zhou, Qibin Liu, Yue Xu, Shu Li
